messages:
samir: Heads-up — we saw a tenant causing steady KV-residency growth over a ~48h run. Not a single big spike, just slow accumulation and lots of evictions for smaller tenants. Dumped some counters below, looking for ideas on fairness.

jia: ugh. can you paste the counters/logs? is it holding large KV entries or many small ones? :thinking_face:

samir: quick profiling snapshot (top lines only):
```
tenant_id, kv_entries, total_kv_bytes, active_residency_pct, evictions/hr
tenant-A, 4300, 1.6GB, 42.1, 2
tenant-B, 120, 45MB, 9.8, 120
tenant-C, 980, 720MB, 19.4, 15
global_kv_heap: 8.0GB
fragmentation_est: ~14%
cache_pages_swapped: 0 (in-memory paging only)
```
Observations: tenant-A holds lots of small KVs with long-lived prefixes (chat sessions), eviction rate on B skyrockets when A grows.

tom: sounds like noisy-neighbor residency — tenant-A wins residency due to high allocation churn and reuse pattern. Two quick options: 1) tenant-scoped quota on residency pages; 2) change eviction policy to tenant-aware weighted LRU (older tenants/low-priority tenants get higher eviction weight). Both need accounting metadata per-tenant on every allocation.

anita: also seeing fragmentation from variable-sized KV. Slab allocator might help but could increase internal wastage. Another approach: periodic compaction pass that coalesces small free spans and reassigns to tenant pools. We should be careful with pause times.

samir: example noisy log for a minute during steady growth:
```
[12:03:01] alloc tenant-A 8KB key=ctx:... token_count=140
[12:03:02] alloc tenant-A 4KB key=kv:... token_count=62
[12:03:05] evict tenant-B 2KB key=ctx:... reason=low_priority
[12:03:06] evict tenant-B 3KB key=history:... reason=age
```
This pattern repeats continuously — not bursts, so our current global LRU + size-agnostic paging favors the high-reuse tenant.

jia: for fairness metrics I'd suggest tracking per-tenant "residency share" over windows and an eviction impact score (evictions_of_other_tenants / tenant_allocations). If score > threshold => throttle allocations or apply soft TTL. Also track 95p stall latency when eviction happens.

tom: can we simulate quickly? I wrote a small sim that replays alloc/expiry and measures eviction fairness. Run locally like:
```
./kv-sim --trace traces/longchat.json --policy tenant-weighted-lru --tenant-quota 0.2
```
This produced ~3x fewer evictions for low-priority tenants in a quick run.

infra-bot: telemetry link https://telemetry.redwood.internal/kvcache/trace/1743789000 (requires SSO) :link:

anita: low-cost mitigations we could deploy fast:
- per-tenant soft quota (X% of cache, burst for short windows)
- eviction weight config by tenant tier
- small compaction pass every 6hrs with time budget
- track fair-share metric in console (for SRE/debugging)

samir: proposed next steps:
1) instrument per-alloc tenant accounting (owner: tom) — small change, critical for everything
2) prototype soft quota + eviction weights in sim first (owner: tom/jia)
3) add fair-share telemetry & dashboard (owner: anita)
4) design compaction with pause budget (owner: infra)

who can pick up #1 and #2? I can take coordination. :eyes:

jia: I'll pair with tom tomorrow for the sim. :thumbsup:

tom: I'll start a branch for tenant-accounting and wire a flag to toggle tenant-aware eviction. won't touch production default until we test.

samir: thanks — I'll add a short RFC for config knobs and console hooks. Keeping an eye on fragmentation numbers, might be separate follow-up.
